$comment: One source of truth for every atlas TI-Toolbox ships in MNI space. tit/atlas/manifest.py is the only reader; tit/atlas/constants.py, tit/catalog.py and the ROI picker all resolve through it, so an atlas is described in exactly one place. Fields: file (basename in this directory), kind ('volume' | 'surface' -- what targeting flow the UI must route it to), template (the MNI template the atlas is defined in), grid (shape and world origin of the shipped volume, verified against MNI152_T1_1mm.nii.gz where it claims the same grid), labels (sidecar LUT/label table), license, attribution, redistribution ('yes' | 'no (<reason>)'), citation, source (exact URL and sha256 of what was fetched, where recorded). 'not_shipped' lists atlases that were removed: a configuration that still names one fails with that entry's reason. See README.md for the full survey and docs/wiki/atlases.md for the user-facing page.

CBIG's 'FSLMNI152_1mm' volume: header checked against MNI152_T1_1mm.nii.gz -- same 182x218x182 shape and affine, so it is on the FSL MNI152NLin6Asym grid, which is also the template SimNIBS's mni2subject warps assume.
